ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
The sound source $S$ and the observer $A$ are both located somewhere on the $x$-axis. The sound source continuously emits pulse sound signals, with a time interval between two signals of $\Delta{t} = 1.0 \, \text{s}$. It is known that the speed of sound propagation in air is $v_P = 340 \, \text{m/s}$, and the air is stationary relative to the ground.

1. If observer A is stationary and the sound source is moving towards observer A with a velocity of $\mathbf{v_{s}}\mathrm{=}20\mathrm{m/s}$, find the time interval $\Delta \mathrm{t}^{\prime}$ between the reception of two consecutive sound signals by observer A. (Round the result to 2 significant figures.)
2. If observer A is moving at a speed of $\mathrm{{\mathbf{v}}_{A}}\mathrm{{=}}4\mathrm{{m}/\mathrm{{s}}}$ along the positive direction of the $\mathbf{X}$-axis, while the sound source is moving towards the observer at a speed of $\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{s}}\mathrm{=}10\mathrm{m/s}$, find the time interval $\Delta \mathrm{t}^{\prime}$ between the successive reception of two sound signals by the observer. (Round the result to 2 significant figures.)

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure, the sound source S is located on the left side of the x-axis, and the observer A is located on its right side; the positive direction of the x-axis is to the right. The arrow of the sound source velocity v_s points to the right, that is, from S toward A; in the second figure/schematic, the observer velocity v_A also points to the right, indicating that A moves along the +x direction. The relevant sound pulses propagate from S on the left to A on the right. Reasoning: It is known that the emission time interval Δt = 1.0 s, and the speed of sound v_P = 340 m/s. 1. A is stationary, and the sound source moves toward A with v_s = 20 m/s. The spacing formed by adjacent pulses in front of A is λ = (v_P - v_s)Δt = (340 - 20)×1.0 = 320 m. When A is stationary, the receiving interval Δt' = λ/v_P = 320/340 = 0.941... s, taken to 2 significant figures as 0.94 s. 2. A moves along the +x direction with v_A = 4 m/s, and the sound source moves toward A with v_s = 10 m/s. The spacing between adjacent pulses is λ = (v_P - v_s)Δt = (340 - 10)×1.0 = 330 m. The relative speed at which the sound wave catches up with A moving to the right is v_P - v_A = 340 - 4 = 336 m/s, so Δt' = λ/(v_P - v_A) = 330/336 = 0.982... s, taken to 2 significant figures as 0.98 s.
